page_intro: Historian of the Cold War, cultural diplomacy, and East-Central Europe at the University of Warsaw.
paragraphs: I am an assistant professor of history at the University of Warsaw. My research focuses on the Cold War, cultural diplomacy, academic exchange, Sovietology, East-Central Europe, and Polish-Ukrainian intellectual relations.

Across these subjects, I am particularly interested in the people and institutions that connected worlds usually described separately: diplomats and academics, policy circles and émigré communities, universities and foundations, the United States and Eastern Europe. Rather than assuming that ideas simply moved from political centers to peripheral recipients, I examine the intermediaries who translated, contested, and repurposed them.

My forthcoming English-language monograph, A History of the Fulbright Program in Poland, 1945–2025: To Build a Republic of Spirit, will be published by Manchester University Press in 2026. It grows out of my Polish-language study Budując Republikę Ducha (2024) and uses academic exchange to rethink the history of Polish-American relations across the Cold War and its aftermath.

I am currently writing East-Central Europe in Cold War America: The Rise and Fall of an Intellectual Concept, a study of how émigré scholars and American institutions created a new intellectual geography of Europe. My other projects concern Jerzy Giedroyc and Zbigniew Brzezinski, the interaction between Kultura and American Sovietology, Ukrainian émigré political thought, Soviet federalism and sovereignty, and the development of Ukrainian and Central-European studies in North America.

My work combines archival research with intellectual, diplomatic, and institutional history. I am especially drawn to moments when categories that later appear stable — “Central Europe,” “the Soviet Union,” “public diplomacy,” or even “academic exchange” — were still uncertain and politically contested.
short_bio: Oleksandr Avramchuk is an assistant professor of history at the University of Warsaw. He specializes in the Cold War, cultural diplomacy, East-Central Europe, Sovietology, and Polish-Ukrainian intellectual relations. His forthcoming book, A History of the Fulbright Program in Poland, 1945–2025: To Build a Republic of Spirit, will be published by Manchester University Press.
